key_insight: StableWorld demonstrates that explicitly prioritizing stability and temporal consistency—via model design and training objectives—enables reliable, long-horizon interactive video generation under dynamic controls (camera moves, text prompts).
problem_solved: Addresses severe instability and temporal degradation (spatial drift, scene collapse) in long interactive video generation so synthesized worlds remain consistent over extended interactions.
method: Introduce a stability-first training framework with temporal-consistency objectives to reduce drift and collapse over long horizons.
Maintain a persistent scene/world representation (long-term memory or latent state) to preserve appearance, geometry and semantics across frames and interactions.
Design an interactive conditioning pipeline that robustly fuses camera motions and text prompts with the world representation for predictable, controllable video synthesis.
impact: Makes interactive video generation far more reliable for long sequences, enabling practical applications in virtual production, simulation, and interactive content creation where temporal coherence and controllability are critical.
